GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node against MagiKnight.cs:57-76. Five MoveStates with matching ids (POWER_SHIELD_MOVE / DAMPEN_MOVE / PREP_MOVE / MAGIC_BOMB / RAM_MOVE -- note the C# local for RAM_MOVE is `moveState5` bound to SpearMove, and the sim keeps the id RAM_MOVE while naming its handler _spear, which is a rename with no cross-file reference and is therefore unobservable per SHARED-FINDINGS section 3). Chain matches exactly: POWER_SHIELD -> DAMPEN -> RAM -> PREP -> MAGIC_BOMB -> RAM (MagiKnight.cs:65-69 vs knights.py:54-58), so DAMPEN and POWER_SHIELD each happen exactly once per combat and the tail is a three-cycle. INITIAL state is POWER_SHIELD_MOVE on both (MagiKnight.cs:75, knights.py:60). No branch state, so no AddBranch integer and no MonsterAi draw.

guards.what: DampenMove's caster set: C# adds a caster and applies the power ONLY if it was absent (MagiKnight.cs:78-96); the sim always applies (knights.py:69-72)
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 28.) DampenPower now models the caster set: add_caster/on_death refcounting with the wasRemovalPrevented guard, expiring only when the set empties (DampenPower.cs:15,41-56,73-76); MagiKnight._dampen fetches-or-creates and calls PowerCmd.apply only on the create path (MagiKnight.cs:78-96). One disclosed, unobservable divergence: add_caster runs after construction rather than before (PowerCmd.apply has no pre-built-instance overload); nothing reads _casters in between. Witness: test/test_monster_tier_families.py::TestDampenCasterSet + the unedited test_glory.py MagiKnight test.  The text it replaced read: MagiKnight.cs:82-92 fetches the target's existing DampenPower, calls AddCaster(base.Creature) on it, and calls PowerCmd.Apply only when it had to create one. DampenPower.AfterDeath then removes the power only once the LAST caster has died (DampenPower.cs:40-54: remove the dying creature from internalData.casters, `if (casters.Count == 0) await PowerCmd.Remove(this)`). The sim has no caster set at all: DampenPower.on_death is `if creature is not self.applier: return` then _expire (powers.py:3176-3186), so the downgrade lifts when the FIRST applier dies, and knights.py:72 applies unconditionally on every cast. Two observables would diverge with two Dampen appliers: the upgrades come back early, and the second apply fires hooks.on_power_amount_changed('dampen', player, 0) (cmds.py:308-311) that C# never fires, because C#'s StackType is PowerStackType.None (DampenPower.cs:22). [on_power_amount_changed call sites re-verified 2026-08-04 at cmds.py:995,1129, was :308-311; same call shape, moved -- this whole passage is superseded history per the issue's Closed 2026-07-30 note above and is retained for record, not as the live verdict.] DORMANT, with the trigger named and checked rather than asserted: `grep -rln DampenPower src/` returns only AbstractModelSubtypes.cs, MagiKnight.cs and DampenPower.cs -- the Magi Knight is the game's ONLY Dampen applier -- and `grep -rln MagiKnight src/Core/Models/Encounters/` returns only KnightsElite.cs, whose GenerateMonsters yields exactly one MagiKnight alongside a FlailKnight and a SpectralKnight (KnightsElite.cs:36-45), matching the sim's KNIGHTS_ELITE (knights.py:151-154, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :129-132, same composition). A single Magi Knight also casts DAMPEN at most once, because nothing in the chain returns to DAMPEN_MOVE. Concrete trigger: a second Dampen applier -- a second MagiKnight in one encounter, or any new model calling PowerCmd.Apply<DampenPower>.
